config.interval_method: 80%: prediction + scale * empirical 10%/90% quantiles of (actual - prediction)/scale of the same model, pooled over earlier non-test origins with target date <= current origin, bucketed by scope (aggregate|product) and horizon (1-7|8-28); falls back to all horizons, then all scopes, if fewer than 25 residuals; lower bound clipped at 0. The latest (operational) forecast may also use test residuals.
config.product_selection: at each origin: stock codes sold on >= 50% of observation-available days in the 182 days ending at the origin, ranked by units in that window, top 5
config.promotion_metric: mean of validation WAPE over {aggregate, products} x {7, 28}; lowest wins, ties go to the simpler model (seasonal_naive, trailing_mean, gradient_boosting)

promotion_reason: Gradient boosting (g3) has the lowest validation promotion metric (mean WAPE over aggregate/products x 7/28 days) = 0.5248; Trailing mean = 0.6456; Seasonal naive = 0.6760. Chosen on validation origins only; the test period did not influence the choice.

models.description: most recent observation-available value on the target weekday at or before the origin; fallback trailing mean
mean of observation-available days in the 28 calendar days ending at the origin

sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss=absolute_error), direct multi-horizon (horizon is a feature), pooled over aggregate + selected products, target and level features divided by an origin-time scale

limitations: Observed sales are not unconstrained demand: no stock-out, inventory or lost-sales data exist in the source.
No prices, promotions, customer aggregates or other exogenous drivers are used.
Days without source records (including almost every Saturday and holiday gaps) are unavailable, not zero; they are forecast but never scored.
The final source day 2011-12-09 is partial and is excluded as an actual.
Only about two years of history: annual seasonality (the November peak) is seen roughly once before the test period.
Holiday closures (e.g. late December) are not modelled; the latest forecast will over-forecast days the business is closed.
Product series are intermittent and contain bulk orders, so product-level WAPE is high and intervals are wide.
Gradient-boosting configuration was chosen among 3 candidates on the same validation folds, which slightly flatters its validation score; the test period is the unbiased check.
